column1: # component-aliases.tsv — classify frames the title grammar cannot.
# build-registry derives kind/family from the "Skai > <Section> ..." title
# convention. Frames named for what they ARE rather than where they live
# ("X accounts - My list - tablet", "Technicals - Buy", "dropdown-3") therefore
# land as kind:non-screen / family:null, which drops them out of families.mjs
# (it skips anything that is not kind:"screen"), out of catalog-view.mjs, and out
# of every audit. They are in the registry but outside the category system.
# This file closes that gap declaratively — same role bugref-aliases.tsv plays
# for deep-linked child ids. Two kinds are assigned here:
#   component — a real design that must be implemented and can be parity-checked.
#               Rolls up into the whale families alongside its screens.
#   scaffold  — Figma canvas furniture (Directory / Notes / Breakpoint /
#               sidebar-open). NOT a design. Recorded explicitly so a later audit
#               does not re-flag it as an unimplemented gap, which is the same
#               reason bugref-aliases.tsv exists.

column1: # The 45 rows this section used to carry here were a workaround: cosmic-slots
# (and its three sibling slot sections) were never added to NON_SKAI_SECTIONS
# in build-registry.mjs, so the grammar demoted every plain design-state title
# ("Load screen - desktop", "Safari A 1") to kind:non-screen and every
# vverify.cosmic-slots.tsv verdict for them loaded, counted, and was silently
# discarded by apply-verify.mjs. Now that the section is in NON_SKAI_SECTIONS,
# the grammar parses those same titles correctly on its own — 29 rows (the 22
# "Load screen ..." states plus the Directory/Breakpoint/Rectangle scaffolding
# that already matches the generic-scaffold pattern every other non-Skai
# section relies on) are gone from here because they are redundant, not
# because they stopped mattering.
# What is left is what the grammar still cannot tell from a real screen:
# `Mines Desktop` (10401-6360) is Mines game art stray on this page's canvas —
# titled like a legitimate desktop state, it would otherwise be counted as one
# of Cosmic Slots' own screens. The rest are art assets whose titles read as
# plain nouns, not design states — the eight reel sprites, the spaceship and
# astronaut rig pieces, and the two card-art pairs (one pair sharing an
# identical duplicate title, the other distinguishing the wrong-bytes art from
# the art the page actually draws) — each carries a distinction in its note
# that a bare "screen" classification would flatten. Every surviving row's
# family is now "Casino > Cosmic Slots", matching the convention build-registry
# derives for the section's own five page frames.
